checked: bin/cedar-service and bin/firefox-cedar derive /opt/t736-cedar-transport-v2 from their own location. ExecStart and read-only cedarc.conf bind use that same private root.
Broker loader paths resolve verified backend v5, WC v5 vendor libraries and parser v27; OMX config is private, AFBC variables cleared, registry under the dedicated runtime directory.

Firefox preload selects the matched v2 client before FFmpeg v7 libraries; FFmpeg resolves the unchanged seven t736_client_* symbols using RTLD_DEFAULT. Both public client/backend headers are byte-identical to v1.
Actual compiled client/broker hashes match their build record; AArch64, client SONAME, broker libcedar_backend dependency and seven public exports verified.

Unit requires media-v29 and cedar_dev; keeps dedicated account/group, strict filesystem, private network/tmp, no capabilities, device allowlist, cgroup memory/task limits and CPU affinity. No Install section or automatic restart. PrivateMounts explicitly retained.
No new MOZ_DISABLE_*_SANDBOX settings or reduced sandbox levels. Test-client override cleared before Firefox exec.

Two shell scripts pass sh -n. Unit verification with the actual path only fails because that /opt path is absent on the build host; syntax copy with ExecStart=/usr/bin/true passes. Existing unrelated host netplan unit permission warning is preserved in the raw log.
deployment_requirements: Install these launchers separately into the transport bin directory, and provide config/gstomx.conf plus config/cedarc.conf. The previously built transport archive contains candidate binaries/sources/tests only, not this new operational layout.
Stop the old broker before starting the matched v2 pair because both use /run/t736-cedar/decoder.sock. Create a new RDD exec, not an already-connected old process.

Launcher does not create/select a private profile or change its preferences. The invoker must use the isolated --no-remote profile with dom.ipc.forkserver.enable=false, as in the existing v1 workflow.
Allowed browser UID remains explicitly 1000, matching the existing board setup; service runs as t736-cedar with t736 group. Runtime account and file ownership checks remain board acceptance work.
limits: Read-only software review does not prove native ARM64 DONTFORK/seals enforcement, RDD sandbox runtime success, correct deployed loader paths or video performance.
Retaining caller LD_LIBRARY_PATH/LD_PRELOAD follows the existing launcher behavior; this review does not assert arbitrary external environments are sanitized.
